input: Start pressed at frame 180 for 6 frames; A held for the whole run
sprite_mode: 8x16, sprite pattern table $1000; OAM stores y-1, so top = y+1
probe: cargo xtask probe "<rom>" --frame N --press 180:start --buttons a --oam oam/N.bin
capture: one headless probe per frame, N = 700..1100 (401 runs, 401 OAM images)
tile_byte: in 8x16 mode the tile byte selects the pair (tile&$FE, tile|$01); bit 0 is ignored

ship.note: 24x16 Vic Viper: three 8x16 body sprites at x, x+8, x+16 plus an 8x16 exhaust flame 4 px behind. The frame is selected by input direction, not by a timer: it was constant for all 401 frames at rest and for every held direction tested.

ring.note: Spinning ring enemy: two 8x16 sprites side by side (16x16). Four phases of exactly 6 frames each, 24-frame cycle. Phases 3 and 4 are the same artwork as 1 and 2 with both flips set and the two sprites swapped. Measured on one object from frame 700 to 757.

bullet.note: Player shot with weapon level 0. Spawns at stored x=87, y=103 (top 104), 7 px to the right per frame, gone after stored x=241 (23 frames) or earlier on an enemy hit. New shot every 21-23 frames while A is held.

enemy_bullet.note: Enemy projectile, separate from the player shot: two 8x16 sprites 8 px apart (16 px wide), 2 px to the left per frame. Seen frames 1011-1060 and 1075-1096.

explosion.note: Two white (palette 0) burst effects were observed. Both start in empty screen space, stay put in world space (x drifts left with the 0.5 px/frame scroll) and have a fixed 5-frame step.

burst_a.note: Two 8x16 sprites 7 px apart (one flipped horizontally); the pair draws a complete ring. Events at 741-755, 761-775, 870-884, 890-904, 996-1010, 1021-1035.

burst_b.note: Debris ring: first two phases are sprite pairs 8 px apart, last two are a single 8x16 sprite. Events at 968-987, 1038-1057, 1065-1084, 1079-1098.

not_clustered: Tiles $31/$33 (attrs $22 and $A2): a separate two-sprite enemy, static for 8-60+ frames while drifting down-left. Identical objects overlap on the same scanlines, so nearest-neighbour tracking lost them; not part of the ring cycle (the ring object ran a full 24-frame cycle with none of these tiles).
Sprites $B7/$B9/$C1/$C3 (ring enemy group table $8EE2..$8EF1, attrs $21) and $59/$5B (red explosion, $8F29/$8F32) are defined in the ROM but never became visible in frames 700-1100.
The $75-$7F and $81-$85 bursts appear where no enemy was visible on the previous frame, so their owner (enemy kill vs. bullet impact) could not be determined from OAM alone.
HUD power-meter sprite ($6D, attr $23, x=248, y=206) is present every frame but is not an animation.
OAM slot indices are not stable across frames (the game rebuilds the buffer in a different order), so objects were clustered by tile family plus position, not by slot.
